rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s answer addresses their demand that he brought no proof: his challenge and disavowal answer the objection rather than leave it unanswered.
rows.anchor: ومن المستبعد جدا أن يهمل النبي هود عليه السلام في دعوته وحجته التعرض للجواب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response supplies a rational proof against the partners’ divinity: Hūd’s disavowal exposes their false godhood and the claim that one harmed him.
rows.anchor: مشتمل على حجة عقلية على بطلان ألوهية الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge, followed by Hūd’s remaining unharmed among them, is also a miraculous sign confirming his message.
rows.anchor: وعلى آية معجزة لصحة رسالة هود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All together” includes both the people and all their idols in the challenge, making the proof of Hūd’s truth and their falsehood more complete.
rows.anchor: مراده تعجيزهم وتعجيز آلهتهم جميعا فيكون أتم دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative could mean Hūd does not fear them even if they can harm him, as in the magicians’ words to Pharaoh; he follows it with reliance on God to rule out that reading.
rows.anchor: لأن يكون المراد به إظهار أنه لا يخافهم وإن فعلوا به ما فعلوا

words: إِنِّىٓ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd explains that his trust is in God, who directs both his affairs and those of his people, removing any implication that the challenge rests on fearlessness alone.
rows.anchor: فذكر أنه متوكل في أمره على الله الذي هو يدبر أمره وأمرهم

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Every creature” means every animal that moves on earth; taking it by the forelock is a figure for complete sovereignty and ultimate power.
rows.anchor: والأخذ بالناصية كناية عن كمال السلطة ونهاية القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being on a straight path means His governance follows one constant, unchanging way of justice and wisdom, vindicating truth when it confronts falsehood.
rows.anchor: وكونه تعالى على صراط مستقيم هو كون سنته في الخليقة واحدة ثابتة غير متغيرة وهو تدبير الأمور على منهاج العدل والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s trust will succeed: God owns and rules him, his people, and every creature, and His just, constant practice is to support His religion and protect Hūd from their harm.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم في نجاح حجتي التي ألقيتها إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd says “my Lord” on the straight path, not “my Lord and your Lord,” because here he seeks protection for himself through his bond of servitude; the earlier wording stated God’s universal rule.
rows.anchor: فإنه في مقام الدعاء لنفسه على قومه يتوقع أن يحفظه الله من شرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s warning answers their final assertion that some idol had harmed him, which signals their settled refusal to believe.
rows.anchor: الدال على أنهم قاطعون على أن لا يؤمنوا به ودائمون على الجحد

words: فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُم مَّآ أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away from faith and obedience, Hūd has delivered his Lord’s message, completed the proof against them, and made their liability binding.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إن تتولوا وتعرضوا عن الإيمان بي والإطاعة لأمري فقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي وتمت عليكم الحجة ولزمتكم البلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will install another people in their place as successors on earth; the human being is God’s vicegerent there.
rows.anchor: أي يجعل قوما غيركم خلفاء في الأرض مكانكم فإن الإنسان خليفة منه في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd had already described his people as successors after Noah, and the replacement wording parallels the Quranic statement that God may remove and replace a people.
rows.anchor: وقد كان عليه السلام بين لهم أنهم خلفاء في الأرض من بعد قوم نوح كما قال تعالى حكاية عن قوله لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported clause is coordinated with an omitted clause: “My Lord will take you away and install another people.”
rows.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن الجملة الخبرية معطوفة على أخرى مقدرة، والتقدير وسيذهب بكم ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot cause God any loss or thwart His will to destroy them; nothing escapes His knowledge or power, since He preserves everything.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه تتمة لما قبله أي لا تقدرون على إضراره بشيء من الفوت وغيره إن أراد أن يهلككم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses other interpretations offered by commentators as too far from the correct reading, without detailing them here.
rows.anchor: وللمفسرين في الآية وجوه أخر بعيدة عن الصواب أعرضنا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming of God’s command means the descent of punishment, more precisely the divine decree that brings the decisive judgment between messenger and people.
rows.anchor: المراد بمجيء الأمر نزول العذاب وبوجه أدق صدور الأمر الإلهي الذي يستتبع القضاء الفاصل بين الرسول وبين قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning follows Hūd’s promise that repentance would bring abundant rain and increased strength, while turning away in sin incurs severe punishment.
rows.anchor: فإنه كان وعدهم أن يستغفروا الله ويتوبوا إليه أن يرسل السماء عليهم مدرارا ويزيد قوة إلى قوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd were prehistoric Arab inhabitants of the peninsula; their history survives only in unreliable tales, and the extant Torah does not mention them.
rows.anchor: عاد قوم هود هؤلاء قوم من العرب من بشر ما قبل التاريخ كانوا يسكنون الجزيرة انقطعت أخبارهم وانمحت آثارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran places ʿĀd after Noah in al-Aḥqāf; the name may be “first ʿĀd,” suggesting a second ʿĀd as well.
rows.anchor: كانوا قوما يسكنون الأحقاف من شبه جزيرة العرب بعد قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were tall, strong, and physically imposing, with advanced urban life, thriving towns, fertile land, gardens, date palms, and crops.
rows.anchor: كانت لهم أجساد طويلة وكانوا ذوي بسطة في الخلق أولي قوة وبطش شديد وكان لهم تقدم ورقي في المدينة والحضارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After enjoying God’s bounty, they developed idolatry, built monuments on every rise and grand structures as if to live forever, and obeyed arrogant tyrants.
rows.anchor: لم يزل القوم يتنعمون بنعمة الله حتى غيروا ما بأنفسهم فتعرقت فيهم الوثنية وبنوا بكل ريع آية يعبثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent their kinsman Hūd to call them to truth, worship of God, rejection of idols, justice, and mercy; he admonished them and made the way clear.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم أخاهم هودا يدعوهم إلى الحق ويرشدهم إلى أن يعبدوا الله ويرفضوا الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a small group believed; most persisted in defiance, called Hūd foolish and mad, and demanded the threatened punishment, to which he replied that its timing belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وأصر جمهورهم على البغي والعناد، ورموه بالسفه والجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a barren, furious wind through adverse days, lasting seven nights and eight days; it left the people fallen like hollow palm trunks and destroyed them all but their dwellings.
rows.anchor: وأرسل إليهم الريح العقيم ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first mistook the cloud approaching their valleys for rain, but it was the very calamity they had demanded; God annihilated them and saved Hūd and the believers by His mercy.
rows.anchor: وكانوا بادئ ما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم استبشروا وقالوا عارض ممطرنا وقد أخطأوا بل كان هو الذي استعجلوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd was from ʿĀd and the second prophet whose struggle against idolatry and suffering for God the Quran narrates; God praises him among the noble messengers.
rows.anchor: وأما هود عليه السلام فهو من قوم عاد وثاني الأنبياء الذين انتهضوا للدفاع عن الحق ودحض الوثنية ممن ذكر الله قصته وما قاساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means that harming the she-camel would bring them a near, hastened punishment.
rows.anchor: أخذهم عذاب قريب معجل، وهذا معنى الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqr of the camel means slaughtering it; dār is a built dwelling place and here denotes their city, while the alternative “the world” is unlikely.
rows.anchor: والدار هي المكان الذي يبنيه الإنسان فيسكن فيه ويأوي إليه هو وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their three days of enjoyment can mean living comfortably in their city or savoring its attractive views, furnishings, food, drink, and freedom to indulge their desires.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتمتعهم في مدينتهم العيش والتنعم بالحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the command to enjoy themselves; “a promise not belied” explains that command.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى قوله { تمتعوا } الخ، و { وعد غير مكذوب } بيان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is elliptic: one reconstruction is “We saved them from the punishment and from that day’s disgrace.”
rows.anchor: فمعطوف على حذوف والتقدير نجيناهم من العذاب ومن خزي يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reconstruction is “We saved them from the people and from that day’s disgrace,” as in the prayer to be saved from the wrongdoing people.
rows.anchor: أو أن التقدير نجيناهم من القوم ومن خزي يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Strong, the Mighty” explains the rescue, and the shift from first-person plural to third-person emphasizes lordship: the people left servitude and rejected their Lord’s bounty.
rows.anchor: والوجه فيه ذكر صفة الربوبية ليدل به على خروجهم من زي العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry seized the wrongdoers, and “jāthimīn” describes those fallen face down.
rows.anchor: جثم جثوما إذا وقع على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Yaghnaw” means they had dwelt there; the pronoun refers to their dwellings.
rows.anchor: غني بالمكان أي أقام فيه، والضمير راجع إلى الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two closing clauses summarize the detailed story: the first its outcome for Thamūd and Salih’s mission, the second God’s recompense, paralleling the close of Hūd’s story.
rows.anchor: فالجملة الأولى تلخيص ما انتهى إليه أمر ثمود ودعوة صالح عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In al-Kāfī, Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh says God never destroys a people before sending messengers to establish proof; Thamūd rejected Salih and demanded a pregnant she-camel from their revered rock.
rows.anchor: في الكافي مسندا عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing al-Kāfī report attributed above to Abū Baṣīr from Abū ʿAbd Allāh says the camel and townspeople alternated water days, and everyone drank its milk on its day.
rows.anchor: فكانت الناقة إذا كان يومها شربت الماء ذلك اليوم فيحبسونها فلا يبقى صغير وكبير إلا شرب من لبنها يومهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report says the people tired of alternating days, commissioned Qudār to kill the camel, and all shared in striking and eating it; its foal fled up the mountain crying three times.
rows.anchor: وأقبل قوم صالح فلم يبق منهم أحد إلا شركه في ضربته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that report, God tells Salih that the people transgressed by killing the harmless sign that benefited them, then offers forgiveness if they repent before a three-day punishment.
rows.anchor: إن قومك قد طغوا وبغوا وقتلوا ناقة بعثها الله إليهم حجة عليهم ولم يكن لهم فيها ضرر وكان لهم أعظم المنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continued report recounts Salih’s warning of yellow, then red, then black faces over three days; the hard-hearted still refuse repentance and their ancestral idols.
rows.anchor: إنكم تصبحون غدا ووجوهكم مصفرة، واليوم الثاني وجوهكم محمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing report attributed above to Abū Baṣīr from Abū ʿAbd Allāh says Gabriel’s scream ruptured their hearing and hearts; all died instantly, and a fire from heaven burned them.
rows.anchor: فلما كان نصف الليل أتاهم جبرئيل فصرخ لهم صرخة خرقت تلك الصرخة أسماعهم وفلقت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extraordinary report details are unobjectionable: the camel itself existed by miracle, and the Quran specifies its alternating water day with the whole town.
rows.anchor: واشتمال الحديث على أمور خارقة للعادة كشرب الناس جميعا من لبن الناقة وكذا تغير ألوان وجوههم يوما فيوما لا ضير فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the cry to Gabriel does not prevent it from being a heavenly thunderbolt whose sound killed and fire burned them; natural events are also assigned to angels.
rows.anchor: وأما كون الصيحة من جبرئيل فلا ينافي كونها صاعقة سماوية نازلة عليهم أماتتهم بصوتها وأحرقتهم بنارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their having prepared camphor and shrouds during the three days is figurative: they had readied themselves for death.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام إنهم قد كانوا في الثلاثة الأيام قد تحنطوا وتكفنوا كأنه كناية عن تهيئهم للموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report that the camel was a mile wide is weakened by the proportions it implies—a nearly three-mile hump—and the implausibility that one man could kill it with a sword; the killer’s act was no miracle.
rows.anchor: وهو مما يوهن الرواية لا لاستحالة وقوعه فإن ذلك ممكن الدفع من جهة أن كينونتها كانت عن إعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel’s day of drinking against the entire town’s day at least suggests that its body was exceptionally large.
rows.anchor: ومع ذلك لا يخلو قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd were ancient Arab inhabitants of Wādī al-Qurā between Medina and Syria; their traces are lost and little can be established about their history.
rows.anchor: ثمود قوم من العرب العاربة كانوا يسكنون وادي القرى بين المدينة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran portrays them as a later Arab nation with settled agriculture, plainside palaces, secure mountain homes, flowing springs, gardens, date palms, and crops.
rows.anchor: ولهم حضارة ومدنية يعمرون الأرض ويتخذون من سهولها قصورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd followed a tribal order led by notables and elders; nine men in the city where Salih was sent spread corruption, worshipped idols, and became excessively rebellious.
rows.anchor: كانت ثمود تعيش على سنة الشعوب والقبائل يحكم فيهم سادتهم وشيوخهم وقد كانت في المدينة التي بعث فيها صالح تسعة رهط يفسدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salih came from a distinguished, respected family and was known for intelligence and competence; he called them to monotheism, abandon idols, justice, and restraint from arrogance and excess.
rows.anchor: وكان من بيت الشرف والفخار معروفا بالعقل والكفاية فدعاهم إلى توحيد الله سبحانه وأن يتركوا عبادة الأصنام وأن يسيروا في مجتمعهم بالعدل والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few weak people believed; the arrogant majority persisted in unbelief, humiliated believers, and called Salih foolish and a sorcerer.
rows.anchor: فلم يؤمن به إلا جماعة قليلة من ضعفائهم وأما الطغاة المستكبرون وعامة من تبعهم فأصروا على كفرهم واستذلوا الذين آمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demanded proof and proposed a she-camel from the mountain rock; Salih brought the sign and assigned alternating water days, free grazing, and a warning against harming her.
rows.anchor: واقترحوا له أن يخرج لهم من صخر الجبل ناقة فأتاهم بناقة على ما وصفوها به

words: فَقَالَ تَمَتَّعُوا۟ فِى دَارِكُمْ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they sent their most wretched man to kill the camel, Salih told them to enjoy their city for three days, a promise that would not fail.
rows.anchor: ثم إنهم طغوا ومكروا وبعثوا أشقاهم لقتل الناقة فعقرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city’s clans plotted to kill Salih and his family, then deny responsibility to their heir; God counter-plotted and struck them with the blast, quake, and cry, while saving the believers.
rows.anchor: ثم مكرت شعوب المدينة وأرهاطها بصالح وتقاسموا بينهم لنبيتنه وأهله ثم نقولن لوليه ما شهدنا مهلك أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After destruction, Salih turned away reproaching them for rejecting his Lord’s message and counsel; the divine announcement declares Thamūd’s disbelief and ruin.
rows.anchor: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present Torah does not mention Salih; he is the third prophet in the Quranic sequence after Noah and Hūd, whom God praises and chooses above the worlds.
rows.anchor: كان عليه السلام من قوم ثمود ثالث الأنبياء المذكورين في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recounts Shuʿayb’s mission to Midian, where idolatry, fraud in weights and measures, and corruption were widespread; the people refused him and persecuted him and his followers until God destroyed them.
rows.anchor: وكان قد شاع التطفيف في الكيل والوزن عندهم واشتد الفساد فيهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet calls Shuʿayb “the orator of the prophets”; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه قال كان شعيب خطيب الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian is the town of Shuʿayb’s people; assigning the mission to the town rather than its inhabitants is figurative attribution, like saying “the gutter ran.”
rows.anchor: ومدين اسم مدينة كان يسكنها قوم شعيب ففي نسبة إرسال شعيب إلى مدين وكان مرسلا إلى أهله نوع من المجاز في الإسناد كقولنا جرى الميزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Shuʿayb their brother indicates that he belonged to their people.
rows.anchor: وفي عد شعيب عليه السلام أخا لهم دلالة على أنه كان ينتسب إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mikyāl and mīzān name the instruments used for measuring and weighing; the measured or weighed goods, rather than the instruments, are what can be deficient.
rows.anchor: المكيال والميزان اسما آلة بمعنى ما يكال به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing deficiency to the measure and scale is a rational/metonymic figure of speech.
rows.anchor: فنسبة النقص إلى المكيال والميزان من المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Short measure is singled out because it was rampant and especially damaging among them, so the admonition emphasizes it among their sins.
rows.anchor: وفي تخصيص نقص المكيال والميزان من بين معاصيهم بالذكر دلالة على شيوعه بينهم وإقبالهم عليه وإفراطهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of “I see you in good” is that they enjoy wealth, ample provision, low prices, and fertility, so they have no need to cheat people for a small illicit gain; this explains the prohibition on short measures.
rows.anchor: وهو ما أنعم الله تعالى عليكم من المال وسعة الرزق والرخص والخصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More broadly, “good” can mean that God cares for them and grants reason, guidance, and provision; this leaves no excuse for idolatry or corrupt dealing and can explain both preceding commands and the warning.
rows.anchor: ويمكن تعميم الخير بأن يراد به أنكم مشمولون لعناية الله معنيون بنعمه آتاكم عقلا ورشدا ورزقكم رزقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible sense is “I look on you with goodwill,” like a compassionate adviser who wants their happiness; the warning about punishment then explains that benevolent concern.
rows.anchor: أني أراكم برؤية خير أي أنظر إليكم نظر الناصح المشفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The all-encompassing day may be Judgment Day or the day of annihilating punishment; its punishment admits no escape, refuge, helper, repentance, or intercession, so it is certain.
rows.anchor: يشير به إلى يوم القيامة أو يوم نزول عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gives two deterrents from disobedience: their existing prosperity removes the need to take others’ property unlawfully, and a surrounding punishment awaits.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما أن وراء مخالفة أمر الله يوما محيطا يخاف عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īfāʾ means giving the full due; bakhs means diminution or shortchanging.
rows.anchor: الإيفاء إعطاء الحق بتمامه والبخس النقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed positive command and prohibition repeat the earlier general warning to stress an essential practice for their society.
rows.anchor: كرر القول في المكيال والميزان بالأخذ بالتفصيل بعد الإجمال مبالغة في الاهتمام بأمر لا غنى لمجتمعهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simply avoiding short measure is insufficient: sellers must give full measure and weight, not reduce people’s goods in transactions, and return what belongs to them as it is.
rows.anchor: بل يجب أن يوفي الكائل والوازن مكياله وميزانه ويعطياهما حقهما ولا يبخسا ولا ينقصا الأشياء المنسوبة إلى الناس بالمعاملة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿayth and ʿathy are close in meaning, like the paired forms jadhb and jadb; ʿayth is commonly sensory corruption, while ʿathy is corruption apprehended in judgment.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب العيث والعثي يتقاربان نحو جذب وجبذ إلا أن العيث أكثر ما يقال في الفساد الذي يدرك حسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms are ʿathā yaʿthā ʿathyan and ʿāthā yaʿthū ʿuthūwan; “spreading corruption” is a circumstantial accusative reinforcing the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا { ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين } وعثا يعثو عثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Spreading corruption” emphasizes the prohibition, like saying “do not corrupt with corruption.”
rows.anchor: لإفادة التأكيد نظير ما يفيده قولنا لا تفسدوا إفسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can independently prohibit all earthly corruption, including killing, injury, and financial, reputational, or honor-based injustice.
rows.anchor: نهي مستأنف عن الفساد في الأرض من قتل أو جرح أو أي ظلم مالي أو جاهي أو عرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause may explain and reinforce the preceding ban on short measure, since fraud in weighing and measuring is itself corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يستفاد من السياق كون الجملة عطفا تفسيريا للنهي السابق فيكون نهيا تأكيديا عن التطفيف ونقص المكيال والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Civil society rests on exchange: every association entails giving and taking, as people cooperate by offering benefit to gain an equal or greater benefit in return.
rows.anchor: إن الاجتماع المدني الدائر بين أفراد النوع الإنساني مبني على المبادلة حقيقة فما من مواصلة ومرابطة بين فردين من أفراد النوع إلا وفيه إعطاء وأخذ
